title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1986 'Analysis situs' combinatorial axiomatics of stratified ('tame') spaces. M is a set of strata, identified with M* ⊂ P(M). F_M ⊂ P(P(M)) is the set of admissible 'M-figures', i.e. sets of strata. The previous page set up the axioms. At*1: stability by intersections. At*2: for A ∈ Φ ∈ F_M there is a smallest figure Φ_A ∈ F_M containing A, so Φ_A ⊂ Φ. At*3: if a family Φ_i ⊂ Φ ∈ F_M is bounded by a figure, its union ∪Φ_i lies in F_M.

This page continues the axioms.
(i) Applying At*3 to the empty family gives ∅ ∈ F_M, as soon as F_M ≠ ∅.
(ii) Af*4 is a pairwise-coherence axiom. For Φ, Ψ ∈ F_M, the union Φ∪Ψ is in F_M iff Φ_A ∪ Φ_B ∈ F_M for all A ∈ Φ, B ∈ Ψ. The inserted gloss says that, by At*3, 'Φ∪Ψ ∈ F_M' just means 'Φ∪Ψ is bounded above (majorée) in F_M'. So joinability of two figures is reduced to joinability of the principal figures Φ_A ('multistrates').
(iii) He then reinterprets Φ_A as the set of sub-strata of A lying in Φ. This gives a sharper form of Af*2: if A ∈ Φ∩Ψ, then the multistrate attached to A in Φ and in Ψ is the same, and it belongs to F_M. In other words, the closure of a stratum is intrinsic and does not depend on the ambient figure.
(iv) Corollary: if Φ ⊂ Ψ are figures, then Φ is closed (down-closed) in Ψ, hence a subfigure Φ ≤ Ψ. Indeed, for A ∈ Φ we have Ψ_A = Φ_A ⊂ Φ.

The next page extracts from this a specialization order on M and a theorem-scholie. That theorem identifies the category of (groupoidal) stratifications (F, ≤, ≪) satisfying At1–At7 with pairs (M, F_M) satisfying the At* axioms. The M-figures become closed sets, and strata correspond to the ∧-irreducible elements.

Abstractly, F_M is a family of down-sets with the following properties:
- each element has a canonical principal closure;
- bounded unions exist;
- consistency (boundedness) of a union is checked pairwise on principal elements.
This is essentially a 'coherent' bounded-complete lattice-like structure, a combinatorial model of the closed-set lattice of a stratified space.
errors: No real error. '∅ ∈ F_M (car F_M ≠ ∅)' is correct only via At*3 applied to the empty family; the argument is left implicit.
Necessity in Af*4 ('il faut et suffit') follows from At*3, since Φ_A∪Ψ_B ⊂ Φ∪Ψ is bounded. Only sufficiency is a genuine axiom.
The notation Φ_B for B ∈ Ψ is justified only after the reformulated Af*2, which shows that the closure is independent of the figure. Logically it is used slightly before being established.

ideas.what: Axiomatising closed unions of strata (figures) as a family of subsets closed under intersections and bounded unions, with principal closures Φ_A
ideas.modern_name: Closure system / Alexandrov (down-set) topology on the face poset of a stratification; cellular/stratified posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937) for poset topologies; stratified-space combinatorics (Thom, Mather, later exit-path/poset-stratified spaces of Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 announces 'topologie modérée' and stratified structures, but not this axiom system

ideas.what: Af*4: union of two figures is a figure iff all pairwise unions of principal figures are figures (pairwise consistency)
ideas.modern_name: Coherence condition (consistency checked pairwise), as in coherent Scott domains / Girard coherence spaces / flag-complex condition

ideas.what: Intrinsic closure: the multistrate Φ_A attached to a stratum is independent of the ambient figure; hence inclusion of figures implies closedness (subfigure)
ideas.modern_name: Closure of a stratum is well-defined / frontier condition; subcomplexes are closed
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in Whitney/Thom stratification theory (frontier condition)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiom system for M-figures contains a pairwise-coherence axiom (Af*4). It makes the poset of figures a coherent, bounded-complete structure, the same shape as Scott/Plotkin coherent domains and Girard's coherence spaces. Girard's coherence spaces appeared in 1987, contemporaneous with these notes. The link between combinatorial models of stratified spaces and domain-theoretic coherence does not seem to be made in the literature.
missed.quote: pour que Φ ∪ Ψ soit dans F_M ... il faut et suffit que pour tout A ∈ Φ, B ∈ Ψ, Φ_A ∪ Φ_B soit dans F_M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor but suggestive bridge between poset-stratified spaces (exit paths, AFT stratifications) and domain theory / coherence-space semantics. Pairwise-checkable gluing is useful for algorithmic or combinatorial descriptions of stratified spaces.

missed.claim: Part of the unpublished combinatorial axiomatics of 'tame' stratified spaces (At1–At7 ↔ At*1–At*4, theorem-scholie on the next page). The axiom list is still being revised here and was never finalized or published.
missed.quote: Je voudrais revenir sur Φ_A ... Af*2 peut se formuler sous la forme plus compréhensible
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This axiom list documents Grothendieck's concrete version of the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse. It could be compared with modern combinatorial definitions of stratified spaces.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine-looking axiom page, but it shows a pairwise-coherence axiom inside Grothendieck's unpublished combinatorial approach to tame stratified spaces, an episode largely absent from the literature. The individual mathematics is elementary.
transcription_corrections: Inserted gloss likely reads '(i.e., par Af*3, soit majorée dans F_M ...)': the image shows 'majoré ... F_M' consistent with At*3's 'réunions majorées', rather than 'pré-F_M'. The trailing underlined words remain uncertain.
First line of Af*4 shows struck-out 'strat.[?]' replaced; 'il faut et suffit' is correct.
Af*2 reformulated: the image reads 'Alors la multistrate associée à A dans Φ, et dans Ψ, est la même, et elle est ∈ F_M' (singular, feminine), not 'les multistrates ... sont les mêmes'.
Axioms on this page are labelled 'Af*' (not 'At*') in the image.
